frequency_question: How often do executive agencies successfully carry out the revocation of recognized accrediting bodies when leadership signals clear intent and capability?
membership_rule: Includes any formal agency action initiated by executive leadership to strip recognition from a major national accreditor. Excludes voluntary relinquishments or minor probationary warnings that did not result in formal termination proceedings.
window: Any comparable multi-year presidential or departmental administration window (e.g., 4-year executive terms).

cases.name: Department of Education review of ACICS recognition (Obama-Trump transition era)
Department of Education review of ABA specialized accreditation scope challenges

coverage_note: 2 named cases covering major federal recognition revocations or near-revocations of professional/institutional accreditors.
known_gaps: Few direct precedents exist for stripping the primary legal accreditor of an entire core profession like law, making the sample size inherently small.
skeleton: Total administrative attempts to strip or severely curtail major institutional/professional accreditors by executive departments since 1990, multiplied by the success rate of those attempts under motivated leadership.
multiplier: 2 attempts identified in recent decades; 1 resulted in successful terminal revocation (ACICS), 1 resulted in settlement/retention (ABA scope narrowing without full revocation).
validity_reason: Tied to the current executive administration's tenure and standard Department of Education regulatory review cycles.
